import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive customer segmentation analysis
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.35, wspace=0.35)

# Calculate total spending and age
df['Total_Spending'] = (df['MntWines'] + df['MntFruits'] + df['MntMeatProducts'] + 
                        df['MntFishProducts'] + df['MntSweetProducts'] + df['MntGoldProds'])
df['Age'] = 2024 - df['Year_Birth']
df['Total_Children'] = df['Kidhome'] + df['Teenhome']

# 1. Income vs Total Spending by Education (scatter plot)
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, :2])
education_order = df.groupby('Education')['Total_Spending'].median().sort_values().index
colors = sns.color_palette("husl", n_colors=len(education_order))
for i, edu in enumerate(education_order):
    subset = df[df['Education'] == edu]
    ax1.scatter(subset['Income'], subset['Total_Spending'], alpha=0.6, 
               label=edu, s=30, color=colors[i])
ax1.set_xlabel('Income ($)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_ylabel('Total Spending ($)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_title('Customer Income vs Total Spending by Education Level', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
ax1.legend(title='Education', fontsize=9)
ax1.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 2. Spending Distribution by Category (box plot)
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
spending_categories = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 
                       'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
spending_data = [df[cat].values for cat in spending_categories]
bp = ax2.boxplot(spending_data, labels=['Wines', 'Fruits', 'Meat', 'Fish', 'Sweets', 'Gold'],
                 patch_artist=True, showfliers=False)
for patch, color in zip(bp['boxes'], sns.color_palette("Set2", 6)):
    patch.set_facecolor(color)
ax2.set_ylabel('Amount Spent ($)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_title('Spending by Product Category', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
ax2.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
ax2.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# 3. Age Distribution (histogram)
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
ax3.hist(df['Age'], bins=30, color='steelblue', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax3.set_xlabel('Age (years)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_ylabel('Number of Customers', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_title('Customer Age Distribution', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
ax3.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# 4. Purchase Channel Comparison (bar plot)
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
channels = ['NumWebPurchases', 'NumCatalogPurchases', 'NumStorePurchases', 'NumDealsPurchases']
channel_means = [df[ch].sum() for ch in channels]
bars = ax4.bar(['Web', 'Catalog', 'Store', 'Deals'], channel_means, 
               color=['#FF6B6B', '#4ECDC4', '#45B7D1', '#FFA07A'], edgecolor='black', alpha=0.8)
ax4.set_ylabel('Total Purchases', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_title('Total Purchases by Channel', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
ax4.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)
for bar in bars:
    height = bar.get_height()
    ax4.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2., height,
            f'{int(height):,}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9, fontweight='bold')

# 5. Marital Status Distribution (pie chart)
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
marital_counts = df['Marital_Status'].value_counts()
colors_pie = sns.color_palette("pastel", n_colors=len(marital_counts))
ax5.pie(marital_counts.values, labels=marital_counts.index, autopct='%1.1f%%',
        colors=colors_pie, startangle=90)
ax5.set_title('Marital Status Distribution', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')

# 6. Spending vs Number of Children (violin plot)
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
sns.violinplot(data=df, x='Total_Children', y='Total_Spending', ax=ax6, palette='muted')
ax6.set_xlabel('Number of Children at Home', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax6.set_ylabel('Total Spending ($)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax6.set_title('Spending vs Number of Children', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
ax6.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# 7. Campaign Acceptance Rate (bar plot)
